nodes.source_text: Cs-corrected TEM revealed a passive film with thickness of about 4-5 nm... A well-defined bi-layer passive film is seen, where the inner (barrier) layer adjacent to the metal is enriched in Cr and depleted in Fe, while the outer (precipitated) layer is depleted in Cr and enriched in Fe. It is noteworthy that the film/matrix interface is sharp, well defined, and straight, even at the atomic level.

nodes.source_text: The passive film formed in chloride-containing H2SO4 solution (condition 2) is shown in Fig. 3c. It is immediately obvious that the previously sharp and straight interface in chloride-free solution has become indistinct and substantially undulating... Cl to be concentrated within the inner layer, (average content ~1 atomic %). Significantly lower amounts of Cl (0.1 atomic %) were detected in the outer layer.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows tri-layer passive film structure immediately after preparation that becomes homogeneous bi-layer oxide after ~6 days air aging via dehydration of outer Fe-rich hydroxide layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1a is the HAADF scanning transmission electron microscopic (HAADF-STEM) image showing the passive film on FeCr15Ni15 single crystal formed in H2SO4 electrolyte... after aging the specimen in air for a few days... the contrast had become homogeneous, following disappearance of the middle darker-contrast layer (Fig. 1b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Super-X EDS mapping confirms bi-layer structure (inner Cr-rich/Fe-depleted, outer Fe-rich/Cr-depleted) in chloride-free films; Cl accumulates primarily in inner layer (~1 at%) with 0.1 at% in outer layer for chloride-containing films.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDS mapping analysis (Fig. 2a) indicates a well-defined bi-layer structure with the inner Cr-rich layer and the outer Fe-rich layer... Cl to be concentrated within the inner layer, (average content ~1 atomic %). Significantly lower amounts of Cl (0.1 atomic %) were detected in the outer layer.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals sharp straight interfaces in chloride-free conditions but indistinct undulating interfaces in chloride conditions; passive films are mostly amorphous (4-5 nm thick) containing embedded 1-3 nm face-centered cubic nanocrystals.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Cs-corrected TEM revealed a passive film with thickness of about 4-5 nm... the previously sharp and straight interface in chloride-free solution has become indistinct and substantially undulating... some periodic two-dimensional lattices with a scale of 1–3 nm are often visualized.

nodes.characterization_summary: LADIA simulation of HAADF-STEM images reveals no lattice distortion for straight interface in chloride-free electrolyte but clear lattice expansion and tensile strain on metal matrix side for undulating interface in chloride-containing electrolyte.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The straight interface formed in chloride-free electrolyte revealed no signs of lattice distortion on the matrix side (Fig. 6a, b). Conversely, the undulating interface formed in chloride-containing electrolyte shows clear evidence of strain-induced lattice expansion on the matrix side (Fig. 6c, d).
